plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers with layered petals. It thrives in partial shade and acidic, well-drained soil, and is a staple of winter gardens in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, peaking in mid-winter
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil, used for centuries in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing tall, sturdy stalks topped with large trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, garden plants bloom in the summer heat, while in the Northern Hemisphere, forced bulbs bloom indoors during winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere; winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to tropical Americas and the Caribbean; grown worldwide, including South Africa, Australia, and as a houseplant in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Although often called amaryllis, true Amaryllis belladonna is a different South African genus; the popular holiday flowers are Hippeastrum hybrids from South America.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of silky bracts surrounding a center of tiny true flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, with peak bloom from late spring through summer
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its ancient lineage predates the breakup of the Gondwana supercontinent.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A hardy evergreen perennial that pushes up cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens in the cold of winter, often through snow. It prefers shaded, humus-rich, alkaline soil.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and Apennines; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts are toxic; flowers are able to survive freezing temperatures thanks to their frost-tolerant tissue.
